newsitem.title: FRANCE: BoF's Marchelli sees room to cut rates carefully.
newsitem.headline: BoF's Marchelli sees room to cut rates carefully.

text.p: Bank of France Monetary Policy Council member Paul Marchelli said on Friday that he still saw room to cut interest rates in France if it were done carefully.
Speaking after the nomination of two new members to the Bank's council, Marchelli said it was impossible to see a change in the council's majority in favour of a weaker franc.
"We still have room for manoeuvre on official rates and we should use it with care," Marchelli told Reuters.
"I do not see a possibility that there will be on the monetary policy council a change in the majority in favour of weakening the franc. It is completely unthinkable," he said.
The French government announced earlier that Pierre Guillen and Jean-Rene Bernard would be named members of the Bank's monetary policy council.
Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said that Guillen and Bernard would replace ex-journalist Jean Boissonnat and ex-banker Bruno de Maulde, whose mandates expire next week, on the nine-member council.
Marchelli said he was pleased with the nominations.
"I am satisfied because I think the monetary policy that we have followed until now will be continued and maybe even accelerated," he said.
He said he hoped rates could come down faster but that such moves depended on "external contingencies" such as international financial markets.
"We would all like to have lower rates faster, but we are serious people," he said, adding that no one on the council took their responsibilities lightly.
He said markets would be wrong to interpret the appointments as a sign that the Bank would abandon the longstanding franc/marc link.
He noted that after the appointments, President Jacques Chirac confirmed his wish to see the Bank continue to conduct a stable and steady monetary policy.
